get_category_info.description: Count what one category holds, without listing any of it. The counts are of direct members only, which is how a workflow decides whether a category is worth walking into before asking for its contents.

parameters.description: The category on Commons, with or without the 'Category:' in front. Categories are how Commons is organised; find one with 'Search categories' or 'Suggest titles'.
parameters.name: category

page_count.description: Gallery and other pages filed here.

get_file_categories.description: List the categories one file is filed under, which is how Commons says what a file is about. Housekeeping categories are hidden on the site and left out here unless asked for.
get_file_categories.display_name: Get the categories a file is in
get_file_categories.name: get_file_categories

parameters.description: The file on Commons. Its name is enough ('Tour Eiffel Wikimedia Commons.jpg'), with or without the 'File:' in front, and a link to the file's page or to the image itself works too.

get_file_details.description: Everything about one file, including how it must be credited. Commons files are free to reuse but nearly all of them ask for attribution, so this returns the licence, the author and the credit line alongside the file's URL, size and dimensions.

parameters.description: The file on Commons. Its name is enough ('Tour Eiffel Wikimedia Commons.jpg'), with or without the 'File:' in front, and a link to the file's page or to the image itself works too.

parameters.description: Which language to return the description and credit in. Commons descriptions are written in many languages at once; a file with none in the language chosen falls back to what it has. Defaults to English.

get_file_revisions.description: List the versions of the file itself, newest first. A Commons file can be re-uploaded over with a crop, a higher resolution or a restoration, and each version keeps its own URL, so a workflow can tell whether the file it recorded is still the one being served.

parameters.description: The file on Commons. Its name is enough ('Tour Eiffel Wikimedia Commons.jpg'), with or without the 'File:' in front, and a link to the file's page or to the image itself works too.

is_current.description: True for the version being served today.

get_file_structured_data.description: Read a file's captions and its Wikidata statements, such as depicts (P180). Commons has been re-describing its files as data rather than prose, and this is the machine-readable half: it says what a photo shows as an item id rather than as a sentence in one language.

parameters.description: The file on Commons. Its name is enough ('Tour Eiffel Wikimedia Commons.jpg'), with or without the 'File:' in front, and a link to the file's page or to the image itself works too.

type.description: item, time, quantity, coordinate, text or string.

get_file_usage.description: List the pages across every Wikimedia project that use this file. Commons is the shared repository behind all of them, so one photo can be on a Wikipedia article in forty languages at once. This is the measure of how widely a file is actually used.
get_file_usage.display_name: Get where a file is used

get_file_wikitext.description: Read the raw wikitext of a file's description page. Everything Commons knows about a file that is not in its structured data is written here in templates, so read it when a workflow needs something the shaped fields do not carry.

get_thumbnail_url.description: Ask Commons to render one file at a given width and return the URL, for embedding it in an email, a document or a message without moving the original. Works for video and PDF too, which are rendered as a first frame or a first page. Commons rounds up to its nearest standard size, so the image served can be a little wider than the one asked for.

get_user_info.description: Look up a Commons contributor: how long they have been here, how active they are and what rights they hold. Read it to check who is behind an upload before reusing their work, or to credit them by the name their account carries.

list_category_files.description: List the files filed directly under one category, each with its URL and a preview. Only direct members: Commons categories nest, so a file in 'Eiffel Tower at night' is not in 'Eiffel Tower'. Walk down with 'List subcategories'.

parameters.description: Read the index by name, or by upload time. The uploader and date filters need one of the time orders.

description: Search Wikimedia Commons for freely licensed photos, video, audio and documents, and read what each one needs to be reused: its URL, a preview at any size, its licence, author and credit line. Browse by category, find files taken near a place, read a file's structured data and where it is used across Wikipedia, and watch what is being uploaded and changed.
